subject.title: docs: LiteLLM supply chain attack advisory (v1.82.7 / v1.82.8)

question: What LiteLLM provider-doc guidance should OpenClaw carry for the March 2026 compromised PyPI releases: current safe install/version guidance, affected-version rollback wording, or only upstream links plus key-rotation steps?
rationale: The missing docs update is narrow, but choosing third-party supply-chain remediation text and a safe install version is a security-maintainer decision because upstream now says affected packages were deleted and current releases are clean while PyPI publishes newer releases than 1.82.6.

options.title: Approve updated advisory wording
options.body: Security maintainers choose current install guidance and affected-version remediation wording, then a focused docs PR updates docs/providers/litellm.md.

options.title: Document only upstream mitigation
options.body: The docs warn about the incident, link upstream LiteLLM/PyPI resources, and advise credential rotation without naming a current safe install version.

options.title: Decline provider-specific advisory
options.body: OpenClaw keeps LiteLLM incident guidance out of core docs and relies on upstream security resources for affected-version details.

recommendation.title: Approve updated advisory wording
recommendation.body: Security maintainers choose current install guidance and affected-version remediation wording, then a focused docs PR updates docs/providers/litellm.md.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the adjacent supply-chain tracker and already framed this LiteLLM incident as part of broader security response work.
